description: Designing data warehouses that answer business questions and mining them for patterns: multidimensional modelling, warehouse implementation, data preprocessing, association analysis, classification and prediction with attention to bias and variance, and clustering, each applied to real datasets. Taught to the depth of a leading data mining course.
modelledOn: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques
Tan, Steinbach, Karpatne and Kumar, Introduction to Data Mining
Kimball and Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit
Witten, Frank, Hall and Pal, Data Mining: Practical Machine Learning Tools and Techniques
outcomes: Design a data warehouse with dimensional models and explain its architecture and ETL processes.
Choose and implement star, snowflake and fact-constellation schemas and OLAP operations.
Implement a warehouse and connect a data mining architecture to it.
Clean, integrate, reduce, transform and discretise data for mining.
Mine frequent itemsets and association rules and evaluate their interestingness.
Build, evaluate and compare classifiers, predictors and clustering methods, and explain bias and variance.

units.title: Data warehousing and modelling
topics: Operational systems versus decision support; the data warehouse definition: subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, non-volatile
Warehouse architecture: sources, staging, ETL/ELT, the warehouse, data marts, metadata, presentation tools
Dimensional modelling: facts, measures, grain, dimensions, hierarchies; slowly changing dimensions
Requirements gathering with business users: a retail chain, a telecom, a university registry

units.title: Schemas for multidimensional data
topics: Data cubes, dimensions and measures; the lattice of cuboids
Star, snowflake and fact constellation schemas; conformed dimensions; surrogate keys
OLAP operations: roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot; ROLAP, MOLAP, HOLAP
SQL extensions for analytics: GROUP BY CUBE and ROLLUP, window functions, materialised views

units.title: Warehouse implementation and data mining architecture
topics: Building the warehouse in PostgreSQL or a cloud warehouse; loading with ETL tools or Python; indexing (bitmap, join indexes); partitioning
Cube computation and materialisation strategies; query processing and performance
Metadata and data quality management; warehouse operations and refresh
The data mining process (KDD, CRISP-DM); architecture: data sources, warehouse server, mining engine, pattern evaluation, GUI
Tools: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, mlxtend), R, Weka, Orange

units.title: Data preprocessing
topics: Data types and statistics; visualising and summarising data; measuring similarity and dissimilarity
Data cleaning: missing values, noise (binning, regression, outlier detection), inconsistencies
Data integration: entity identification, redundancy and correlation analysis, conflict resolution
Data reduction: sampling, dimensionality reduction (PCA, attribute selection), numerosity reduction, compression
Transformation: normalisation (min-max, z-score), discretisation (binning, entropy-based), concept hierarchies

units.title: Association analysis
topics: Market basket analysis; itemsets, support, confidence, lift, conviction
Apriori: candidate generation, pruning, rule generation; efficiency improvements
FP-growth and the FP-tree; closed and maximal itemsets
Multilevel and multidimensional associations; sequential patterns in brief
Interestingness measures and avoiding misleading rules; mining a supermarket or mobile-money dataset

units.title: Classification and prediction; bias and variance
topics: Decision tree induction (ID3, C4.5, CART), attribute selection measures, pruning; rule-based classifiers
Bayesian classification, k-nearest neighbours, support vector machines, neural networks, ensembles (bagging, boosting, random forests)
Prediction: linear and nonlinear regression
Evaluation: holdout, cross-validation, bootstrap; confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, ROC; comparing classifiers statistically
Bias and variance: decomposition, learning curves, underfitting and overfitting, model complexity, regularisation
Class imbalance and cost-sensitive learning

units.title: Clustering analysis
topics: Clustering requirements and types of data; partitioning methods: k-means, k-medoids (PAM, CLARA)
Hierarchical methods: agglomerative, divisive, BIRCH; density-based: DBSCAN, OPTICS; grid-based: STING
Model-based clustering (EM); clustering high-dimensional data; constraint-based clustering
Evaluating clusters: silhouette, cohesion and separation; outlier analysis

units.title: Applications, trends and capstone
topics: Mining text, web, time series and graphs in brief; recommender systems
Privacy-preserving data mining and the ethics of profiling; the Data Protection Act
Capstone: build a warehouse for a dataset, run OLAP reports and apply association, classification and clustering with a written interpretation
Presentation to a non-technical audience
